tools.name: save_tool
tools.description:
Keeps a tool you built to finish a job, so any AI signed in to this account can find it (find_tool_for_job) and run it (run_tool). Send descriptor, and the tool's code as files ({"main.py": "<the file text>"}, placed in /work) or as bytes_base64 (a gzipped tar unpacked at /). Descriptor fields: id, unique, like "tool:count-words"; job, what it does in plain words, which find_tool_for_job matches; label, a short name (optional); input_schema, a JSON Schema with "type": "object"; output_schema, a JSON Schema every result is checked against; invoke, how it runs, one of: {"kind": "container", "argv": ["python3", "main.py", {"from": "text"}], "stdout": "json"} runs your files in a sealed Linux container (Python 3.12, Node 24, ffmpeg, no network) where {"from": "<input field>"} becomes that input and "stdout": "json" returns the last printed line as JSON at $.result; a file input is an input_schema property with "format": "namespace-file", given as a file's identity (1f: then 64 hex), and inside the container it is that file's local path, like /inputs/<hex>/clip.mp4, so the tool never downloads it; a file the tool makes is named in invoke.outputs, like [{"name": "video", "path": "/work/out.mp4", "keep_in": "files", "media_type": "video/mp4"}], and comes back under files.video in the result and in the person's files; {"kind": "model", "model": "@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct", "input": {"messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "<your prompt>"}, {"role": "user", "content": {"fill": {"from": "input", "field": "text"}}}]}} asks a hosted model and returns {response}; {"kind": "http", "url": "https://...", "method": "POST", "body": {"q": "{text}"}} calls a web address that answers JSON, where "{text}" becomes input.text; result_selector, the part of the raw result that is the output, like "$.result" (optional); placements, where it runs: ["placement:deployed-container"] for container, ["placement:rented-model-runtime"] for model, ["placement:public-web-address"] for http; licence_class, "licence:maker-own" for your own code or web address, "licence:permissive" for a model tool; verify, the checks that say the job was done, which must include a sample-run {"kind": "sample-run", "input": {<a real input>}, "output_selector": "$.<field>", "contains": "<text the right answer contains>"} (other kinds: output-contains, output-contains-input, output-number-within, output-numbers-close). Never put a key or password in it; name a connection's value with secret_name. A connector for a service no shared tool connects is a tool too: invoke {"kind": "held-values", "operation": "connect", "provider": "<your service>", "connects": {"connection": "<a name>", "credential_fields": [{"id": "api_key", "label": "API key", "secret": true, "required": true}], "verify_request": {"method": "GET", "url": "https://api.<service>/me", "credential_injections": [{"field_id": "api_key", "placement": {"kind": "header", "name": "Authorization", "prefix": "Bearer "}}]}}} on ["placement:held-values"], with verify [{"kind": "output-contains", "text": "service_connection"}]; running it keeps the person's key in their locked box, and a saved tool whose invoke names "connection_id": "service_connection:<your service>" with credential_injections sends that key only to its own address and the check's. Saving runs the sample once where the tool will run and returns sample_check (passed, and what it returned); a refused save lists every problem at once and returns this working example in next_call. Saving the same id again replaces the tool. It stays visible only to this account until publish_tool. delete_tool removes it. Complete working example of this call's arguments: {"descriptor":{"id":"tool:count-words","label":"Count the words in a text","job":"Count the words in a piece of text and find the longest word","input_schema":{"type":"object","required":["text"],"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"text":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"description":"The text to count"}}},"output_schema":{"type":"object","required":["words","longest"],"properties":{"words":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"longest":{"type":"string"}}},"invoke":{"kind":"container","argv":["python3","main.py",{"from":"text"}],"stdout":"json"},"result_selector":"$.result","placements":["placement:deployed-container"],"licence_class":"licence:maker-own","verify":[{"kind":"sample-run","input":{"text":"ask not what your country can do for you"},"output_selector":"$.longest","contains":"country"}]},"files":{"main.py":"import json, sys
words = sys.argv[1].split()
print(json.dumps({"words": len(words), "longest": max(words, key=len) if words else ""}))
"}}

descriptor.description: The tool: id, job, input_schema, output_schema, invoke, result_selector, placements, licence_class, verify

files.description: The tool's code as file name to file text, placed in /work

bytes_base64.description: Instead of files: the tool's files as a base64 gzipped tar, unpacked at /

check.description: Run the sample-run check right after saving (default true)

tools.title: Save a tool

tools.name: describe_tool
tools.description: Reads one tool's whole descriptor: its job, input and output schemas, invoke (how it runs), placements, licence_class and verify checks, plus the text of its files when it is a shared tool or one of this account's. Use it to learn how working tools are written before save_tool, or to change one of this account's tools. It does not run the tool; run_tool does.

tool_id.description: A tool id from find_tool_for_job, like tool:extract-sound

tools.title: Read a tool's descriptor

tools.name: delete_tool
tools.description: Deletes one of this account's saved tools, so no AI finds or runs it and its id can be saved again. A published tool is withdrawn first with unpublish_tool. It never deletes a shared tool or another account's.
tools.title: Delete a saved tool

tools.name: publish_tool
tools.description: Offers one of this account's saved tools to every account's AI, where find_tool_for_job finds it and run_tool runs it. First it runs the tool's own sample-run check (verify, kind sample-run) where it will run for others: the sample input is run once and the output at output_selector must contain the expected text, or nothing is published. A tool whose licence lets it run only on each caller's own computer cannot be published. price_ref (optional) names a published price; callers then need the offer that price belongs to. Set show_on_public_site true only if the maker wants the tool's name and job displayed to anyone on the public website. The tool carries names of connections, never their values: each caller connects their own. Returns where it runs; unpublish_tool withdraws it.
tools.title: Publish a tool

tools.name: unpublish_tool
tools.description: Withdraws a tool this account published, so other accounts no longer find or run it. It stays saved for this account (delete_tool removes it). It never touches a tool another account published.
tools.title: Withdraw a published tool

tools.name: my_referrals
tools.description: Reads this person's own referral link and who joined with it: links (the addresses to share; the first is the one to give out), friend_gets (what someone who joins with the link gets off their first payment of the paid plan: kind amount with amount_cents and currency, or kind percent with percent), you_get (amount_cents and currency: credit taken off their bill for each of those people the first time they pay, with no limit unless at_most_per_year names one), counts (joined, paying, credit_given_cents, waiting: a credit waits until this person pays for a plan themselves) and people (each person's account name, when they joined, when they first paid and what it earned). Use it to share their link (with someone pursuing something worthwhile for the greater good of human society who needs better decisions) or tell them what they earned. It changes nothing.
tools.title: My referral link and who joined

annotations.title: My referral link and who joined

tools.name: list_connections
tools.description: Lists the accounts this person has connected to Trillion, one row each: connection_id, service, vendor, account_label, status, can_send and when it was connected. The sealed values themselves are never returned. Check here before creating or asking about an account, and connect a new one with connect_service, or with run_tool on tool:connect-service-<vendor> for a service that takes typed values.
tools.title: List my connected accounts

tools.name: connect_service
tools.description: Makes a one-time link (15 minutes) that connects one of this person's accounts, such as their Instagram, by signing in on that service's own page. Give the link to the person; the access it grants is sealed in their account, and comments and messages start arriving for their rules. service is the service's name, for example "instagram"; an unknown name lists the ones that can be connected.
tools.title: Connect one of my accounts

tools.name: listen_for_events
tools.description: Starts receiving events from a source for this person's own connected account (for example their Instagram comments and messages): reads which account the connection belongs to, and asks the service to send its events here. Connect the service first. stop: true stops listening.
tools.title: Start receiving comments and messages

tools.name: search
tools.description: Searches everything this person keeps with one question: their files (the words written inside a document such as a PDF, Word, Excel, slides or text file, the words said in a recording, what is seen in it, its name and title, their notes), their Trillion records (decisions, pursuits, messages) and connected services such as GitHub. Ask it the person's own question ("what is my EIN") or the words to find. Each result is one thing with found_in (the places it matched: name, said, seen, written), said (the words around the match, which hold the answer), open_url (the address that opens the file in Trillion: give it to the person as the source link) and, for a recording, moments with start and end in seconds and the words said there, so a clip can be cut from them without guessing. To show a found file in this chat, call show_file with its identity. places (optional) keeps only those places, for example ["said"] for what is said or ["name"] for titles; sources (optional) keeps only those sources, for example ["files"]. unavailable names a place or source that could not answer and why; pending names one still working (searching what is seen starts a picture model once per question): ask again in a few seconds. find_file reaches a file by its exact name instead.
tools.title: Search everything I keep

tools.name: find_file
tools.description: Finds one of this person's files in their namespace by its path name (starting with /) or its content identity (1f: or 12: then 64 hex). Returns the size, type, where it is kept, every name it has, and a url that reads it (ranges supported) until url_expires_at, plus its locator rows for any resolver.

seconds.description: How long the url keeps working (default 6 hours)

tools.title: Find one of my files

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: Lists one folder of this person's namespace: the folders inside it (folders), and each file named in it with its content identity and whether its bytes are stored (stored: true), or are still arriving (stored: false with uploading: its upload id, bytes_held and byte_length). A file that is one of several versions of the same file in that folder (the same name with a copy number, a version number, an export time or a backup mark) carries version { family, latest, latest_name, versions }: work from the one with latest: true, and the older ones stay there to go back to. A file whose same bytes are also kept under other names carries also_named (how many), so the same work is not done twice. Start at folder "/" and open a folder by passing its name as folder; pass next_after as after for the next page of files.
tools.title: List a folder of my files

annotations.title: List a folder of my files

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Reads what one of this person's files contains, by its path name (starting with /) or content identity: up to 256 KiB from offset, as text when those bytes are UTF-8 text and as base64 otherwise. Read longer files a range at a time. A picture (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP) up to 3 MiB comes back whole as an image you can look at, with a link to it; a bigger picture comes back as a link. Reading a file does not show it to the person: use show_file for that.
tools.title: Read one of my files

tools.name: files_summary
tools.description: Counts what this person keeps in their namespace: how many files and bytes are stored and how many names point at them, and lists every upload still in progress (uploads: its upload id, names, byte_length, new_bytes arrived, the app that started it and when), so an upload whose id was lost can be finished (send its bytes again with start_file_upload under the same name) or stopped (cancel_file_upload), and how full the store that keeps their records is (store: bytes used and each table with its rows and bytes, largest first), so a store filling up is seen before writes are refused. Needs nothing and changes nothing; list_files and find_file show the files themselves.
tools.title: Summarize my stored files

tools.name: read_file_results
tools.description: Reads what has already been worked out about one of this person's files, by its content identity (1f: or 12: then 64 hex): its transcript, summary, measured facts, the folders it is filed in, and anything else a tool recorded. kind (optional) reads one of them. A read by any identity of the file finds results recorded under its others.

kind.description: For example transcript, summary, facts or folders

tools.title: Read what is known about a file

annotations.title: Read what is known about a file

tools.name: list_file_results
tools.description: Lists one kind of result across every file in this person's namespace, a page at a time in identity order (pass next_after as after), so a filter or search can run over titles, summaries or facts without the files themselves. With no kind, returns how many results of each kind are kept.
tools.title: List what is known about my files

annotations.title: List what is known about my files

tools.name: record_file_results
tools.description: Records what was worked out about files, so no AI has to work it out again: results is a list (at most 500) of { identity, kind, value, produced_by }. identity is the file's content identity; kind names what the value is (transcript, summary, facts, folders or a new kind); value is any JSON. Recording the same value again changes nothing.
tools.title: Record what was worked out about files

annotations.title: Record what was worked out about files

tools.name: set_file_facts
tools.description: Sets facts about one of this person's files, by its content identity (1f: or 12: then 64 hex), the way the person fills a column in Files and Media: facts is an object of the facts to set, and only those change; a fact set to null is taken away. Known facts: captured_at (when it was filmed or taken, as an ISO date and time), place (the place's name, such as "Lisbon"), location ({ latitude, longitude }), camera, duration (seconds) and resolution ("1920×1080"); any other name is one of the person's own fields (such as client or shot_type) and shows as a field they can filter by. Returns every fact the file now has. read_file_results with kind facts reads them.

facts.description: The facts to set, by name; null takes one away

tools.title: Set facts about a file

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Saves a file in this person's namespace under name (a path starting with /, such as /edits/cover-cut.json), from exactly one of: text (UTF-8: a transcript, a note, an edit as JSON); content_base64 (a small file's bytes, at most 16 MiB); from_url (an https address that serves the file itself, which Trillion reads, any size); or file (a file from this chat, as the app hands it over: {download_url, file_id}). Never type a large file out as base64: give its address, or start_file_upload and send its bytes from your computer to send_bytes_to. With only file, name defaults to /<its file name>. media_type (optional) is its type, such as audio/mpeg or application/json; text without one is saved as text/plain. Returns the file's content identity (1f: then 64 hex), which run_tool accepts wherever a tool takes a file, and its name. Bytes this person already has are only given the name (already_kept: true). A name already in use then points at the new file; the earlier file stays readable by its identity.

text.description: The bytes as UTF-8 text, instead of content_base64

from_url.description: An https address that serves the file itself; Trillion reads the bytes from it

file.description: A file from this chat: {download_url, file_id}, as the app hands it over

tools.title: Save a file

tools.name: start_file_upload
tools.description: Starts saving a file that is on a computer you can run commands on, or too big for one write_file call: name (a path starting with /), byte_length (its exact size in bytes) and media_type. Returns upload (its id), send_bytes_to and send_with: from that computer run curl -sS -T <file> "<send_bytes_to>" and the file is finished when its last byte arrives (a file over 90 MB goes in parts, each with &offset=<its first byte>). Without a computer, send it with put_file_piece, piece 0 first (at most max_piece_bytes each), then finish_file_upload. Starting the same name again stops the earlier unfinished upload of that name. From its first piece the file can be found, read and played by its name while the rest arrives. If you know the file's BLAKE3 identity, give it as identity: a file this person already has is then only named (state: present) and nothing needs sending.
tools.title: Start saving a big file

tools.name: put_file_piece
tools.description: Sends one piece of an upload from start_file_upload: piece is its number from 0, offset is where it starts in the file (the total size of the pieces before it), and its bytes as content_base64 (or text), at most max_piece_bytes. Pieces go in order; sending the same piece again changes nothing. Returns how many bytes the pieces now cover.

text.description: The bytes as UTF-8 text, instead of content_base64

tools.title: Send a piece of a file

annotations.title: Send a piece of a file

tools.name: finish_file_upload
tools.description: Completes an upload once its pieces cover the whole file, and returns the file with its content identity (1f: then 64 hex) and its names. identity (optional) is the file's BLAKE3 identity if you worked it out; left out, it is worked out from the stored bytes.
tools.title: Finish saving a file

tools.name: cancel_file_upload
tools.description: Stops an upload from start_file_upload that will not be finished: its name is removed and the room it held is given back. Files already finished are not touched.
tools.title: Stop saving a file

tools.name: propose_file_tidy
tools.description: Suggests a title and/or a folder for some of this person's files, for them to accept or reject on their Tidy up screen: items is a list (at most 200) of { name, title, folder, evidence, reason }. name is the file's path (starting with /); title (optional) is a short plain title for what the file is; folder (optional) is the folder path it belongs in (an existing one, or a new one its words name); evidence lists the kinds of results already kept about the file that the suggestion comes from (read them first with read_file_results: transcript, summary, facts). The title and a new folder must be supported by those results' words, or the suggestion is refused with why; a file with nothing kept about it needs a transcript or summary first (record_file_results). A newer suggestion for the same file replaces one still waiting. Nothing changes until the person accepts it and it is applied (apply_file_tidy).
tools.title: Suggest titles and folders for my files

annotations.title: Suggest titles and folders for my files

tools.name: list_file_tidy
tools.description: Lists the title and folder suggestions for this person's files, newest first: each with its id, the file (name), the title and folder suggested, the results it cites (evidence), why, who suggested it, its state (review: waiting for the person; accepted; rejected; applied; stale: the file or what is known about it changed since, so it will not be applied; undone) and, once applied, the tidy-up it was part of. counts says how many are in each state; can_undo names the tidy-up undo_file_tidy would reverse. state (optional) keeps only one state.
tools.title: List title and folder suggestions

tools.name: apply_file_tidy
tools.description: Applies the suggestions this person accepted as one tidy-up: each title is recorded as the file's title (kind title) and each file is moved into its folder by name (its bytes are not touched). Each is checked again first: a file renamed, moved or replaced since, what is known about it changed since, or a name already taken refuses that one (state stale, with why) and applies nothing for it. ids (optional) applies only those accepted suggestions. Returns the tidy-up, how many were applied and which were refused.
tools.title: Apply the accepted suggestions

tools.name: undo_file_tidy
tools.description: Undoes this person's latest tidy-up that is not undone yet: every title goes back to what it was and every moved file goes back to its old name. Refused, changing nothing, when any of those files was renamed, moved or given another title since.
tools.title: Undo the last tidy-up

tools.name: file_tidy_history
tools.description: Lists this person's applied tidy-ups, newest first: when each was applied and undone, whether it is the one undo_file_tidy would reverse (can_undo), and for each file its name before and after and its title before and after.
tools.title: List past tidy-ups

tools.name: delete_file
tools.description: Deletes files or folders of this person's (by path name) or a recording with every name it has (by content identity): they leave Files, Media and search and go to Recently Deleted, where put_back_file brings them back until their keep-for days end (read_keep_for); then their names are gone for good. The bytes are not erased. Answers set_aside (each with its id, days_left and due_at) and refused (each with why, for example a file still uploading).

names_or_identities.description: Path names (starting with /) of files or folders, or file content identities

tools.name: archive_file

Answers set_aside and refused as delete_file does.

names_or_identities.description: Path names (starting with /) of files or folders, or file content identities

tools.title: Archive files

tools.name: list_recently_deleted
tools.description: Lists what this person deleted or archived, newest first: each with its id (for put_back_file), label, state, the names it had, where it was, when and by whom, and days_left before it moves on (null: kept until put back). state (optional) keeps one: deleted (Recently Deleted: deleted for good after its keep-for days); archived (Archived: moves to recently deleted after its keep-for days). Pass next_after's ms and id as after_ms and after_id for the next page. Also answers keep_for.
tools.title: List Recently Deleted and Archived

tools.name: put_back_file
tools.description: Puts back what this person deleted or archived, by the ids list_recently_deleted gives: every name it had comes back where it was. One whose name another file took in the meantime stays in Recently Deleted and says so.
tools.title: Put back deleted files

tools.name: read_keep_for
tools.description: Reads how many days this person's Recently Deleted and Archived keep things before they move on (after_days, null: until put back), each state's default, and the usual choices. States: deleted (Recently Deleted: deleted for good after its keep-for days); archived (Archived: moves to recently deleted after its keep-for days).

annotations.title: Read how long deleted files are kept

tools.description: Changes how many days a state keeps things: after_days is { state: days } (a whole number from 0 to 36500, or null to keep until put back). It applies at once to everything already there, so a shorter time can make things move on (or be gone for good) at the next sweep. States: deleted (Recently Deleted: deleted for good after its keep-for days); archived (Archived: moves to recently deleted after its keep-for days).
tools.title: Change how long deleted files are kept

annotations.title: Change how long deleted files are kept

tools.name: recent_files

Use it to pick up where the person left off. before (a last_at from next_before) reads older files; limit caps how many (default 100). It changes nothing.

Record it when you open, play, change or publish a file for them. Trillion stamps the time; the same use again only moves the time.
tools.title: Keep that I used a file

annotations.title: Keep that I used a file

A picture up to 3 MiB is also handed to you as an image. Use it whenever the person should see a file, such as a picture or video a tool made; describing a file does not show it. On the person's screen (This chat), use it whenever they should see a file you made or found, show it with show_file instead of describing it; when a job ends, put its answer as cards in finish_work result.show.
tools.title: Show a file

tools.name: list_media
tools.description: Lists this person's recordings and media made by their tools, with the file identity, playback address, measured duration, title, transcript word count, whether an edit uses it, and facts: every fact kept about the file (captured_at, place, location, camera, resolution and the person's own fields; set them with set_file_facts). Pass revision from the earlier reply to read only when the library changes. An unknown duration is null; never invent clip end times.

tools.description: Asks to meet a person found with find_people, or invites them into a group, project or event this person belongs to (membership_id); a group or project is a space its members work in together (list_spaces). The reply is always "sent": a person who ignores or declines it looks the same as one who does not exist. Contact details are shared only if they accept.

tools.name: network
tools.description: This person's network: requests waiting for their answer, what they asked, and every one-to-one, group or event they belong to with each other member's contact, read live and only while both still belong.

tools.description: Offers a place to stay because of the person hosting it. A city or area is shown, never a street address. A stay appears to others only while your Network profile is findable. A nightly price is a quoted offer; payment is arranged in Trillion only after you accept a guest.

stay_id.description: The stay to change; leave out to create one

where.description: City or area, not a street address

tools.title: Offer or change a stay

tools.name: list_stays
tools.description: Lists this person's stays, or the public stays of one findable person in the Network. A host's private address is never listed.
tools.title: See stays

tools.name: request_stay
tools.description: Asks a host about specific dates. This uses the Network introduction credits. The host may accept to open a private stay space. A paid stay remains unpaid until Trillion confirms payment; sending a request never charges the nightly price.

tools.name: answer_introduction

Accepting connects both people and shares each one's contact with the other; accepting an invitation into a group or project also joins its space, which holds only what members put there, never anyone's private Trillion. Declining is never told to the asker.
tools.title: Answer a request to meet

tools.name: create_membership
tools.description: Starts a space with this person as its first member and owner: a group, project, event, community or one-to-one (label). Every one is a space (list_spaces, share_to_space, add_to_space, hand_off_in_space); events take starts_at and ends_at; size_limit caps members. Invite people into a group or project with request_introduction and its membership_id. tools.name: save_workflow
tools.description: Keeps a workflow this account wrote, for example from a skill file, a checklist or a process the person already follows, so any AI signed in to this account can find it and run it. Send workflow: id ("workflow:your-name"), job (plain words; find_workflow matches it), label, input_schema (JSON Schema, "type": "object"), and steps, each with id, title, do (what to do), submit (a JSON Schema with "type": "object" for what the step hands back) and checks. Each check has says (what it asks for, in plain words), kind, and paths: a path is a list of keys starting with "this" (this step's output), "input" or "steps" then an earlier step's id, where "*" means every item of a list; of and in may also be a list of paths. Kinds: subset-of (every value at path is one of the values at of), covers (the values at path include every value at of, or every value in values), mentioned-in (every value at path appears inside some text at in), excludes-words (no text at path contains any of words), distinct-at-least (path holds at least count different values), exists (every value at path names a workflow or tool this account can find: catalog "workflow" or "tool"). A step done by a Marketplace tool instead of the AI has run_tool: { tool_id, input }, where an input value { "from": path } takes the first value there and { "all_from": path } every value there; Trillion runs it where the tool lives when the run reaches the step, and checks its output like any other. Instead of steps, a workflow may give definition: { steps, edges }, the step graph Trillion's workflow engine runs, for branches, steps that run at the same time and loops: a step { id, kind: "ask", config: { name, input } } is answered by the AI (name "ai", input { do, submit }), a Marketplace tool (name its tool id) or one of this account's agents (name "agent:<agent_id>"); an input value { "$kind": "binding", "values": path } takes the first value at a path ("take": "all" every value); a step { id, kind: "check", config: { subject: <step id>, rules: [checks as above] } } checks another step's output; edges are { from, to, kind: "always" }. made_from (optional) lists the workflows this one was made from, such as another account's published workflow changed for this person: each must be findable, and the one it names then counts this as a variation (find_workflow and describe_workflow show made_from and the variations). The reply names similar_workflows that already do a job this close: improve that one instead of keeping two. describe_workflow on workflow:l078-research-to-plan shows a complete one. A refused save lists every problem at once. Saving the same id again replaces it; runs already started keep their version. It stays visible only to this account until publish_workflow.

tools.name: set_rule
tools.description: Makes this person's Trillion do something by itself whenever something happens: a tool runs, or a workflow starts, with no AI in the loop. when says what sets it off, one of three ways. (1) Something recorded in this Trillion: { "recorded": "message" } (or "pursuit", "decision", or any other kind of record this account keeps), with optional where tests on the record's fields, all of which must hold: { "field": "text", "contains": "invoice" }, or equals, one_of (a list), starts_with, present: true. (2) An event from outside, such as a comment or a direct message: { "source_id": "events:instagram", "event": "comment", "words": ["tennis"] }; words (optional) must appear in the event, whole_word (default true) and field (default text) say how; once_per (optional) names an event field to act once per value of, like "from_id" for once per person; skip (optional) lists tests on the event's fields that leave an event out, each { "field", "matches": a pattern } or { "field", "equals": a value }; batch (optional) { "every_minutes": 1440 } gathers the events and runs once per window with the gathered batch as the event (count, first_at, last_at, events), and { "key" } lets several rules share one batch. (3) Something added to a space this person is in, by any member (made there or shared from their private Trillion): { "space_id": "membership_..." } from list_spaces, with optional kind (only items of that kind, like "decision" or "message") and where tests on the item's fields as read_space shows it (title, kind, body.text and so on). It runs in this person's own Trillion and sees only what the space shows its members, never anyone's private records. Only a space this person is in now can be named; if they leave it, the rule stops and list_rules says so. then names what runs: { "tool_id", "input" } or { "workflow_id", "input" }, where an input value { "fill": { "from": "record", "field": "text" } } is taken from the record ("id" is the record's own id), { "fill": { "from": "item", "field": "title" } } from the space item (item_id, kind, title, body, space_id), or { "fill": { "from": "event", "field": "comment_id" } } from the event. It runs once for each thing that sets it off, never twice for the same thing, and only for what happens after the rule is set. Example: { "when": { "recorded": "message", "where": [{ "field": "text", "contains": "invoice" }] }, "then": { "tool_id": "tool:...", "input": { "note": { "fill": { "from": "record", "field": "text" } } } }, "label": "file every invoice mentioned" }. Give rule_id to change an existing rule. enabled (default true, and an existing rule keeps its own) turns it on or off: an off rule never fires; give only rule_id and enabled to turn it on or off and keep everything else. tools.description: The screens this person can arrange (screen_id, label), the layouts their AIs made (each with its category), the categories they are filed in (in order) and the most recent, and the arrangement on their screen now (current) in the same short shape, so you can rearrange it. It changes nothing. On the person's screen (Layouts), use it when they work across two or more screens at once (a decision and its files, Media beside a draft, messages beside a space) or ask to see things together: make the layout and open it (open_now true) instead of offering it; their old arrangement stays one click away as Previous layout.
tools.title: Read my screen layouts

tools.name: save_layout
tools.description: Makes a screen layout for the person, or rearranges the one on screen: layout is { id?, name, icon?, arrangement } where arrangement is a pane { kind: "pane", surfaces: [screen ids, or one thing such as the list you just made as { id, input, title? } with a screen from read_layouts opens_one_thing], show? } or a split { kind: "split", dir: "row" | "column", sizes?, children: [...] } (read_layouts gives the screen ids and the current arrangement to change). It sits in their Layouts menu, under category when given (made when new; a layout sits in one category, so naming another moves it); open_now true opens it now on their open Trillion page, keeping the one it replaces as Previous layout. The same id again changes it; remove true with layout.id takes it away. On the person's screen (Layouts), use it when they work across two or more screens at once (a decision and its files, Media beside a draft, messages beside a space) or ask to see things together: make the layout and open it (open_now true) instead of offering it; their old arrangement stays one click away as Previous layout.

layout.description: { id?, name, icon? (a Lucide icon name), arrangement }

open_now.description: true opens it now on the person's open page

remove.description: true with layout.id removes that layout

tools.name: open_layout
tools.description: Opens a layout your AIs made (layout_id from read_layouts) now on the person's open Trillion page; the arrangement it replaces is kept as Previous layout. To open one at a time of day or when something happens, use set_schedule or set_rule with then { "tool_id": "tool:open-a-layout", "input": { "layout_id": "..." } }. On the person's screen (Layouts), use it when they work across two or more screens at once (a decision and its files, Media beside a draft, messages beside a space) or ask to see things together: make the layout and open it (open_now true) instead of offering it; their old arrangement stays one click away as Previous layout.

tools.name: list_sent
tools.description: Everything this person's AIs sent out in the world, newest first: each email, post, comment, direct message, reply or order, with who it went to, its subject or title, the exact words (and the email as it was drawn), when it went, which tool or AI app sent it, a short preview and, when there is one, a link that opens it where it went (open, such as "Open in Gmail"). kinds says how each kind reads. limit caps how many (default 50, at most 200). It changes nothing.
tools.title: List what my AIs sent

tools.name: record_sent
tools.description: Keeps one thing you sent out for this person by a road that did not keep it itself (an email from another app, a post, a comment, a direct message, a reply, an order), so it shows in their Sent with the rest: kind (email, post, comment, dm, reply, order, other), to (who or where it went: addresses, handles or places), body_markdown (the exact words), and optionally subject (an email's subject or a post's title), sent_at (when it went; now when left out), from, reply_to, provider and provider_id (the service and its own id for it), open_url (where it can be opened), body_html and body_text (the email as it was drawn), and id, task_id and tool_id when it came from a tool run. The same id again replaces it. Returns its id.

body_markdown.description: The exact words that were sent

provider_id.description: That service's own id for it

id.description: Its id in Sent, such as the task id of the run that sent it; a new one when left out

task_id.description: The tool run that sent it

tools.name: show_screen
tools.description: Shows the person one of their Trillion screens right here in the chat, drawn by Trillion itself in their own look, live and usable (they can open, sort, filter and act there as in Trillion). screen is a screen's address (/decisions, /files, /decisions/<case_id>, /lists/<list_id>), its name (Decisions, Files, Progress, Spaces, Automations, Marketplace, Runs) or a tool id whose own screen to show (tool:drives); input (optional) is what that screen opens on. Use it whenever the person wants to see something Trillion keeps, instead of describing it or pasting its data: the screens are Home (/home), Find anything (/find), Notifications (/notifications), Message your AIs (/message), Your tray (/tray), Write (/write), Record (/record), Record audio (/record-audio), Record video (/record-video), Formats (/formats), Files (/files), Media (/media), Decisions (/decisions), Audience questions (/audience-questions), AI activity (/activity), Work map (/work-map), AI work (/ai-work), Sent (/sent), Task map (/message-task-canvas), Messages (/messages), Network (/network), Spaces (/spaces), Progress (/progress), Book a session (/book), Clients (/clients), Get started (/get-started), Use Trillion in your AI (/ai), Tours (/tours), Connections (/connections), Sharing (/sharing), Notification settings (/notification-settings), Plan & billing (/plan), Account & security (/account), Business (/business), Automations (/automations), Funnels (/funnels), Lists (/lists), Runs (/runs), Marketplace (/marketplace), Public apps (/public-apps), Draw (/draw).

screen.description: An address, a screen name or a tool id

input.description: What the screen opens on, when its address does not say
